subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should maintainers accept the native `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`/`node-pty` dependency graph and MXC SDK argv-carried config boundary for this prerelease Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: The branch appears to be a plausible first-party external plugin, but the dependency graph and sandbox config transport are security-boundary choices that automation should not approve.

options.title: Approve after parity fix
options.body: Require the registration-mode parity fix and then have maintainer/secops approve the exact head dependency graph if the MXC preview boundary is acceptable.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer merge until MXC offers a non-argv config transport or clearer security guarantees.

options.title: Decline first-party plugin
options.body: Close or redirect the work if maintainers do not want to own this Windows sandbox backend as an official plugin.

recommendation.title: Approve after parity fix
recommendation.body: Require the registration-mode parity fix and then have maintainer/secops approve the exact head dependency graph if the MXC preview boundary is acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: They raised the latest unresolved OpenShell/MXC parity and security-boundary acceptance request on the live PR.
